22420: Etects of hypolimnetic oxygenation on the food resources and feeding ecology of cisco in Amisk Lake, Alberta A\though the ability of hypolimnetic oxygenation to enhance cold-water fish populations in deep eutrophic lakes depends, in part, on the availability of prey, studies that evaluate both fish diets and prey distributions during treatment are rare. Our study compares the diet of cisco Coregonus artedi with the composition and distribution of prey in the two-basin Amisk Lake during the summers of 1989 and 1992, when one of the basins received hypolimnetic oxygenation. Higher dissolved oxygen (DO) concentrations enabled cisco in the treated basin to feed throughout the water column and incorporate hypolimnetic and benthic prey species into their diets, whereas cisco in the reference basin ate primarily epilimnetic prey species. As a result, similarity in the composition of fish diet, which was high in early summer and fall, decreased through mid-summer when differ ences in DO concentrations between the two basins were most pronounced. Although fish prey increased during oxygenation, {ish biomass also increased and resulted in a substantial reduction in per capita food levels; the amount of food in fish stom- achs in 1989 was at least 30 times as high as in 1992. These results demonstrate that if combined with controlled fish exploita- tson to maintain per capita food levels, oxygenation can be a useful tool for improving cold-water fish production. 22422: : Conservation strategies for the recovery of depleted populations of West Indian rock iguanas West Indian iguanas are the world’s most endangered lizards, primarily as a result of habitat degradation and exotic species. | Because relatively healthy populations of Cuban iguanas (Cyc/ura nubila) still exist, this species provides an ideal model for de. veloping conservation strategies that can be applied to other more endangered forms. 22423: Snake blood obtained by tail sticks may not accurately reflect circulating blood Blood samples were taken from tails of brown water snakes Nevodia taxispilota. Three to 5 ml of blood was obtained using a 25 gauge needle attached to a 5cc syringe. The needles were inserted into the ventral aspect of the tail, 5-8 cm posterior to the vent. The needle was inserted at a 45 degree angle and pushed until the needle was in contact with the vertebrae. The needie was then pulled back 2-4 mm and then a gentle vacuum was created with the syringe. The blood was then centrifuged with a hand operated centrifuge. Samples from 25 snakes were examined. Blood samples from 20 of the snakes looked nor mal in color (deep red) and, after centrifugation, had a well defined layer of packed blood cells. Three samples appeared dilute and had a small layer of packed cells following centrifugation. Two other samples were clear, containing no red bloods cells. We have not determined if clear fluid represents lymph or cerebrospinal fluid. Reports in the literature describe major yinph vessels surrounding the blood vessels in the tail of snakes. We suggest that the hematocrit be determined on every blood | sample obtained by tail stick to determine the degree of dilution of the sample. (Poster Session 1, Friday 1:30-5, Saturday $9)

22425: Molecular phylogenetics of the Thamnophiini (Colubridae) and the evolution of pray capture The Thamnopini is a large, ecologically diverse tribe of North American colubrid snakes. The group includes garter snakes, water snakes, crayfish snakes, as well as a number of less well-known genera. Species within tha tribe taka a wida rarga ct both terrestrial and aquatic prey, including fish, tadpoles, frogs, worms, slugs, crayfish, insect larvaa, and small mammals The effects of prey type on strike kinematics are poorly known. The surrogate method permits construction of a habitat suitability model using the sister sce- cies, the Alabama darter, Etheostoma ramseyi. This model incorporates multivariate statistical methods which identifies vari- ebles (e.g., discharge, habitat type, dominant substrate type, water pH, conductivity, temperature, relative abundance) that wal be entered into a GIS spatial database. This model will then be tested on the surrogate prior to its application on the target sce- cies. Thus it is possible to construct a species recovery plan within the context of the species requirements, and compare ex- pected results against field observations obtained with minimal sampling. 22491: Large, long-live fishes often produce millions of eggs during a single spawning season and reproduce over many years. For all this productivity, only two offspring, on the average, must Survive to sexual maturity for the population to be maintained. This implies that in most years an individual will produce no offspring that reach sexual maturity. Yet, some offspring are preduced every year and, while a given year class may not be abundant some portion of these survive to adulthood. This could result in genetic differences among year classes due to limitations on effective population sizes. this phenomencn has become known as the Hedgecock Effect. This paper will present genetic data on species with short (spotted sea trout and weakfish) and long (red drum and wreckfish) life spans that demonstrate this effect. 22495: Chemical cues and the plasticity of life history characteristics in amphibians A wide variety of amphibians exhibit anti-predator behavior when exposed to chemical cues released from injured conspecifics or potential predators. Most studies have documented short term behavioral responses that occur immediately following de- tection of the chemical cues. In a series of experiments we examined the effects of repeatedly exposing amphibian prey to chemical predation risk cues (i.e. alarm cues and predator odors). Both larval anurans and salamanders altered characteristics of their life history (i.e. time to and size at metamorphosis) in response to repeated exposure to these cues. We have evidence that prey species may respond to cues of potential predators if the predators have eaten the prey’s conspecifics, but not if the predators have eaten a different diet. Adaptive plasticity in life history characteristics can also be observed in relation to hatch- ing characteristics. In response to repeated exposure to chemosensory predation risk cues, anuran embryos hatch faster than in the absence of predation risk. Our results demonstrate that repeated exposure to predation risk cues can dramatically alter the life history characteristics of the prey species. (Session 81, Tuesday July 1, Kane 1170, 2:30)

22496: Zebra mussels impede lake trout reproductive success in Lake Michigan Efforts to restore lake trout in the Great Lakes have succeeded in establishing sizable adult populations, but reproduction by stocked lake trout is limited in the lower four lakes. Evidence of spawning and fry hatching has been found at multiple sites lakes-wide; however, all of these sites are in shallow water (<15 m) and many of the most heavily used sites are man-made, i.e., they are breakwalls or water intake structures. We examined lake trout spawning success at an old breakwall which was heavily fouled with zebra mussels, and on three nearby, newly constructed, submerged barrier structures in southwestern Lake Michigan. Lake trout spawned immediately on the newly built structures. The number of eggs deposited and number of fry hatched on unfouled (new) substrate were over two orders of magnitude higher than on fouled substrate. Damage to eggs appeared to be higher on the fouled substrate. Eggs were also eaten at this site by carp. Use of artificial reefs in shallow water to promote lake trout spawning may incur high mortality due to the vulnerability of such locations to exotic predators (carp, ale- wives, and gobies), and biofouling by zebra mussels. These observations raised the hypothesis that the levels of reproductive isolation reached by sympatric ecotypes are controlled by the potential for niche partitioning in different lakes. In this context, the objectives of this study were 1) to assess whether the extent of genetic diver gence ohserved hy mtDNA analysis is confirmed at nuclear loci, and 2) to quantify the extent of trophic niche partitioning be- tween sympatric forms in lakes where different levels of reproductive isolation is reached. Nuclear DNA divergence was esti- mated at 10 microsatellite loci, Ecological niche partitioning was characterized by comparing spatio-temporal distributions, mor phological traits and diet between ecotypes from two lakes. Microsatellite results were fully congruent with the trend that was observed at the mtDNA level, that is, genetic divergence was highest between the most morphologically specialized sympatric ecotypes.
